svg.title: Consumer and producer interceptors: consumer
svg.desc: Offsets 44 and 45 of ticket-orders pass through an IncomingInterceptor on their way to charge(order). For offset 44, afterMessageReceive runs first, then charge() charges order 42 and returns. The connector acks the record, and only then does onMessageAck run. For offset 45, afterMessageReceive runs first again, then charge() throws because CardGateway answers 503. The connector nacks the record and writes it to ticket-orders-dlq, and then onMessageNack runs with the exception. An application log lists each call in the order it ran.
svg.text: One IncomingInterceptor wraps every message on the ticket-orders channel, which uses failure-strategy=dead-letter-queue.

g.text: The connector polls offset 44 from ticket-orders. The record carries X-Correlation-Id 9b2e.
afterMessageReceive gets the message before charge() does. This one logs the offset and the correlation id.
charge() receives the message that afterMessageReceive returned, and charges order 42.
charge() returns, so the message is acked. onMessageAck runs once the connector has handled the ack.
Offset 45 takes the same path: afterMessageReceive first, then charge().
CardGateway answers 503 and charge() throws. 45 is nacked and goes to ticket-orders-dlq, then onMessageNack runs.
Each record gets afterMessageReceive before charge(), then either onMessageAck or onMessageNack.

svg.text: Sources: smallrye.io/smallrye-reactive-messaging (intercepting incoming and outgoing messages, Kafka failure management).
